%20back%2C%20how%20joint%20velocities%20become%20endpoint%20velocities%20through%20a%20matrix%20called%20the%20Jacobian%2C%20and%20why%20the%20endpoint%20accelerates%20in%20ways%20that%20no%20single%20joint%20does.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Read%20it%20in%20order%20and%20run%20each%20cell%20as%20you%20reach%20it.%20Where%20you%20find%20a%20**Challenge**%20or%20a%20set%20of%20**Guiding%20questions**%2C%20stop%20and%20answer%20on%20a%20scratchpad%20before%20moving%20on.%20Several%20of%20them%20ask%20you%20to%20predict%20a%20result%20*before*%20the%20code%20prints%20it.%20Make%20the%20prediction%3B%20a%20wrong%20guess%20that%20the%20code%20then%20corrects%20teaches%20more%20than%20a%20right%20one.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Along%20the%20way%20there%20are%20also%20**Exercises**%2C%20each%20followed%20by%20a%20collapsed%20solution.%20Try%20the%20exercise%20first%2C%20and%20open%20the%20solution%20only%20to%20check%20your%20answer.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20You%20will%20need%20vectors%20from%20%5BScalar%20and%20vector%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fscalar_vector.py)%2C%20derivatives%20from%20%5BKinematics%20of%20a%20particle%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_particle.py)%2C%20and%20the%20tangential%20and%20normal%20accelerations%20from%20%5BPath%20frame%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fpath_frame.py).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Put%20your%20hand%20flat%20on%20a%20table%20and%20slide%20your%20fingertip%20along%20a%20straight%20line%2C%20from%20close%20to%20your%20chest%20to%20almost%20arm's%20length%2C%20without%20moving%20your%20trunk.%20Pay%20attention%20to%20your%20shoulder%20and%20your%20elbow.%20Does%20each%20of%20them%20rotate%20in%20one%20direction%20only%3F%20At%20a%20constant%20rate%3F%20Write%20down%20your%20answers%3B%20the%20checkpoint%20questions%20ask%20you%20to%20come%20back%20to%20them.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Reaching%20in%20a%20straight%20line%0A%0A%20%20%20%20When%20people%20move%20the%20hand%20from%20one%20point%20to%20another%20on%20a%20table%2C%20the%20hand%20travels%20along%20a%20nearly%20straight%20path%2C%20and%20its%20speed%20rises%20and%20falls%20in%20a%20smooth%2C%20bell-shaped%20curve%20(Morasso%2C%201981).%20Flash%20and%20Hogan%20(1985)%20showed%20that%20these%20paths%20are%20well%20described%20by%20the%20*minimum-jerk*%20trajectory%2C%20the%20smoothest%20possible%20movement%20of%20the%20hand%20between%20the%20two%20points%20(see%20%5BThe%20minimum-jerk%20hypothesis%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fminimum_jerk_hypothesis.py)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20straight%2C%20smooth%20path%20is%20simple%20to%20describe%20for%20the%20hand.%20It%20is%20not%20obviously%20simple%20for%20the%20joints.%20The%20shoulder%20and%20the%20elbow%20are%20hinges%3B%20each%20of%20them%20can%20only%20swing%20the%20parts%20beyond%20it%20around%20a%20circle.%20Somehow%2C%20two%20circular%20motions%20must%20add%20up%20to%20a%20straight%20line.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20By%20the%20end%20of%20this%20notebook%20you%20will%20compute%20exactly%20what%20the%20shoulder%20and%20elbow%20have%20to%20do%20for%20such%20a%20reach%2C%20and%20see%20that%20the%20simplicity%20of%20the%20hand's%20movement%20is%20not%20shared%20by%20the%20joints.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%200.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20For%20the%20hand%20to%20move%20in%20a%20straight%20line%2C%20must%20both%20joints%20rotate%20in%20the%20same%20direction%3F%20Must%20they%20rotate%20at%20constant%20angular%20velocities%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20An%20arm%20with%20two%20joints%20moving%20in%20a%20plane%20has%20two%20angles%20to%20set%2C%20and%20the%20hand%20has%20two%20coordinates.%20For%20a%20given%20point%20on%20the%20table%2C%20how%20many%20different%20arm%20configurations%20put%20the%20hand%20there%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Suppose%20the%20elbow%20is%20locked%20and%20the%20shoulder%20rotates%20at%20a%20constant%20angular%20velocity.%20The%20joints%20do%20not%20accelerate.%20Does%20the%20hand%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20SymPy%20derives%20the%20expressions%2C%20NumPy%20evaluates%20them%20and%20Matplotlib%20draws%20the%20plots.%20SymPy%20prints%20derivatives%20with%20respect%20to%20time%20as%20%24%5Cfrac%7Bd%7D%7Bdt%7D%5Ctheta(t)%24%3B%20the%20function%20%60show%60%2C%20defined%20below%2C%20prints%20them%20instead%20in%20%5BNewton's%20notation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FNotation_for_differentiation)%2C%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%24%2C%20which%20is%20much%20easier%20to%20read.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%20%20%20%20import%20sympy%20as%20sym%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.vector%20import%20CoordSys3D%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.physics.mechanics%20import%20dynamicsymbols%0A%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22axes%22%2C%20labelsize%3D12%2C%20titlesize%3D13)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22xtick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D10)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22ytick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D10)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22legend%22%2C%20fontsize%3D10)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20CoordSys3D%2C%20dynamicsymbols%2C%20np%2C%20plt%2C%20sym%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20show(expr%2C%20lhs%3D%22%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Display%20a%20SymPy%20expression%2C%20with%20time%20derivatives%20in%20Newton's%20notation.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20marimo%20as%20mo%0A%20%20%20%20from%20sympy.physics.vector.printing%20import%20vlatex%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20mo.md(rf%22%24%24%20%7Blhs%7D%20%7Bvlatex(expr)%7D%20%24%24%22)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20What%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%3E%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FKinematic_chain%22%3E%3Cimg%20align%3D%22right%22%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fupload.wikimedia.org%2Fwikipedia%2Fcommons%2F2%2F2c%2FModele_cinematique_corps_humain.svg%22%20width%3D%22240%22%20style%3D%22margin%3A%200%2010px%200%2010px%22%20alt%3D%22human%20body%20modelled%20as%20a%20kinematic%20chain%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fa%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**A%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20an%20assembly%20of%20rigid%20bodies%20(links)%20connected%20by%20joints%3B%20it%20is%20the%20mathematical%20model%20for%20a%20mechanical%20system%2C%20which%20in%20turn%20can%20represent%20a%20biological%20system%20such%20as%20the%20human%20body**%20(%5BWikipedia%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FKinematic_chain)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20term%20chain%20refers%20to%20the%20fact%20that%20the%20links%20are%20constrained%20by%20their%20connections%20to%20other%20links%2C%20typically%20by%20a%20hinge%20joint%2C%20also%20called%20a%20pin%20joint%20or%20revolute%20joint.%20As%20a%20consequence%20of%20this%20constraint%2C%20each%20link%20of%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20in%20a%20plane%20rotates%20about%20its%20joint%3A%20the%20motion%20of%20a%20planar%20chain%20is%20built%20out%20of%20circular%20motions%20of%20rigid%20objects.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Chapter%2016%20of%20Ruina%20and%20Pratap's%20book%20and%20chapter%202%20of%20Rade's%20book%20are%20a%20good%20formal%20introduction%20to%20the%20circular%20motion%20of%20a%20rigid%20object%2C%20and%20sections%202.7%20and%202.8%20of%20Rade's%20book%20cover%20kinematic%20chains%20specifically.%20In%20this%20notebook%2C%20however%2C%20we%20do%20not%20use%20the%20formalism%20introduced%20in%20those%20chapters%2C%20the%20rotating%20reference%20frame%20and%20the%20rotation%20matrix%3B%20those%20are%20covered%20in%20%5BRigid-body%20transformations%20in%202D%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ftransformation_2d.py).%20Here%2C%20we%20describe%20the%20kinematics%20of%20a%20chain%20in%20a%20Cartesian%20coordinate%20system%20using%20only%20trigonometry%20and%20calculus.%20This%20approach%20is%20simpler%20and%20more%20intuitive%2C%20but%20it%20gets%20too%20complicated%20for%20a%20chain%20with%20many%20links%20or%20in%20three%20dimensions%3B%20for%20such%20problems%2C%20rigid-body%20transformations%20are%20the%20recommended%20tool%20(see%2C%20for%20example%2C%20Siciliano%20et%20al.%20(2009)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20derive%20the%20kinematic%20properties%20of%20the%20chains%20algebraically%20with%20%5BSymPy%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsympy.org%2F)%2C%20a%20Python%20library%20for%20symbolic%20mathematics.%20SymPy%20has%20a%20%5Bmechanics%20module%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.sympy.org%2Flatest%2Fmodules%2Fphysics%2Fmechanics%2Findex.html)%20built%20for%20deriving%20the%20equations%20of%20motion%20of%20multibody%20systems%2C%20but%20we%20will%20derive%20most%20of%20it%20ourselves%2C%20to%20understand%20the%20details.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cp%20style%3D%22text-align%3A%20right%3B%22%3E%3Ci%3EFigure.%20The%20human%20body%20modelled%20as%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20(%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FKinematic_chain%22%3Eimage%20from%20Wikipedia%3C%2Fa%3E).%3C%2Fi%3E%3C%2Fp%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Properties%20of%20kinematic%20chains%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20**base**%20of%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20the%20extremity%20(origin)%20of%20the%20chain%20that%20is%20typically%20considered%20attached%20to%20the%20ground%2C%20to%20the%20body%2C%20or%20otherwise%20fixed.%20The%20**endpoint**%20is%20the%20other%20extremity%2C%20which%20typically%20can%20move.%20In%20robotics%2C%20the%20term%20**end-effector**%20is%20used%2C%20and%20it%20usually%20refers%20to%20the%20last%20link%20of%20the%20chain.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20topological%20terms%2C%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20called%20**open**%20when%20there%20is%20only%20one%20sequence%20of%20links%20connecting%20its%20two%20ends.%20Otherwise%20it%20is%20called%20**closed**%2C%20and%20a%20sequence%20of%20links%20forms%20a%20loop.%20A%20kinematic%20chain%20can%20be%20**serial**%2C%20**parallel**%2C%20or%20a%20**mix**%20of%20both.%20In%20a%20serial%20chain%20the%20links%20are%20connected%20one%20after%20the%20other%3B%20a%20serial%20chain%20is%20an%20open%20chain.%20Otherwise%2C%20the%20chain%20is%20parallel%2C%20or%20branched%20(for%20example%2C%20the%20hand%20and%20fingers).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Although%20this%20definition%20is%20clear%20and%20classic%20in%20mechanics%2C%20it%20is%20not%20the%20one%20used%20by%20health%20professionals%20(clinicians%20and%20athletic%20trainers)%20to%20describe%20human%20movement.%20They%20call%20a%20set%20of%20joints%20and%20segments%20a%20closed%20or%20open%20kinematic%20(or%20kinetic)%20chain%20simply%20according%20to%20whether%20the%20distal%20segment%2C%20typically%20the%20foot%20or%20the%20hand%2C%20is%20fixed%20(closed%20chain)%20or%20not%20(open%20chain).%20The%20two%20definitions%20sometimes%20classify%20the%20same%20movement%20differently.%20A%20person%20standing%20on%20one%20leg%2C%20for%20example%2C%20is%20an%20open%20kinematic%20chain%20in%20mechanics%2C%20but%20a%20closed%20one%20in%20the%20clinical%20sense.%20In%20this%20text%20we%20stay%20consistent%20with%20mechanics%2C%20but%20keep%20the%20difference%20in%20mind%20when%20talking%20with%20clinicians%20and%20athletic%20trainers.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Another%20important%20property%20of%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20its%20number%20of%20**%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FDegrees_of_freedom_(mechanics)%22%3Edegrees%20of%20freedom%20(DOF)%3C%2Fa%3E**.%20In%20mechanics%2C%20the%20degrees%20of%20freedom%20of%20a%20system%20are%20the%20number%20of%20independent%20parameters%20needed%20to%20define%20its%20configuration.%20A%20particle%20in%203D%20space%20has%20three%20DOFs%2C%20because%20we%20need%20three%20coordinates%20to%20specify%20its%20position.%20A%20rigid%20body%20in%203D%20space%20has%20six%20DOFs%3A%20three%20coordinates%20of%20one%20of%20its%20points%20to%20specify%20its%20position%2C%20and%20three%20angles%20to%20specify%20its%20orientation.%20A%20link%20attached%20to%20a%20fixed%20body%20by%20a%20hinge%20joint%20in%20a%20plane%20needs%20only%20one%20angle%20to%20define%20its%20configuration%2C%20so%20it%20has%20one%20DOF.%20A%20kinematic%20chain%20with%20two%20links%20in%20a%20plane%20has%20two%20DOFs%2C%20and%20so%20on.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20**mobility**%20of%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20its%20total%20number%20of%20degrees%20of%20freedom.%20The%20**redundancy**%20of%20a%20kinematic%20chain%20is%20its%20mobility%20minus%20the%20number%20of%20degrees%20of%20freedom%20of%20the%20endpoint.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20The%20kinematics%20of%20a%20one-link%20system%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20start%20with%20a%20system%20made%20of%20one%20planar%20hinge%20joint%20and%20one%20link.%20Technically%20it%20is%20not%20a%20chain%2C%20but%20it%20introduces%2C%20one%20at%20a%20time%2C%20all%20the%20concepts%20we%20will%20need.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fonelink.gif%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D350%20alt%3D%22one%20link%20attached%20to%20a%20fixed%20body%20by%20a%20hinge%20joint%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20One%20link%20attached%20to%20a%20fixed%20body%20by%20a%20hinge%20joint%20in%20a%20plane.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20need%20a%20Cartesian%20coordinate%20system%20and%20the%20symbols%20for%20time%2C%20%24t%24%2C%20the%20length%20of%20the%20link%2C%20%24%5Cell%24%2C%20and%20the%20joint%20angle%2C%20%24%5Ctheta%24%2C%20which%20is%20a%20function%20of%20time%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(CoordSys3D%2C%20dynamicsymbols%2C%20sym)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20G%20%3D%20CoordSys3D(%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20t%20%3D%20sym.Symbol(%22t%22)%0A%20%20%20%20ell%20%3D%20sym.Symbol(%22ell%22%2C%20real%3DTrue%2C%20positive%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20theta%20%3D%20dynamicsymbols(%22theta%22%2C%20real%3DTrue)%20%20%23%20or%20sym.Function(%22theta%22)(t)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20G%2C%20ell%2C%20t%2C%20theta%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Using%20trigonometry%2C%20the%20position%20of%20the%20endpoint%20in%20terms%20of%20the%20joint%20angle%20and%20the%20length%20of%20the%20link%20is%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(G%2C%20ell%2C%20sym%2C%20theta)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20r_p%20%3D%20ell%20*%20sym.cos(theta)%20*%20G.i%20%2B%20ell%20*%20sym.sin(theta)%20*%20G.j%20%2B%200%20*%20G.k%0A%0A%20%20%20%20show(r_p%2C%20r%22%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D_P%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(r_p%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20With%20the%20components%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(G%2C%20mo%2C%20r_p)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_components%20%3D%20r_p.components%0A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.vstack(%5Bshow(_components%5BG.i%5D%2C%20%22x_P%20%3D%22)%2C%20show(_components%5BG.j%5D%2C%20%22y_P%20%3D%22)%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Forward%20and%20inverse%20kinematics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Computing%20the%20configuration%20of%20a%20link%20or%20a%20chain%2C%20including%20the%20location%20of%20the%20endpoint%2C%20from%20the%20joint%20parameters%20(joint%20angles%20and%20link%20lengths)%2C%20as%20we%20have%20just%20done%2C%20is%20called%20%5B**forward%20or%20direct%20kinematics**%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FForward_kinematics).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%20the%20coordinates%20of%20the%20endpoint%20are%20known%2C%20for%20example%20because%20they%20were%20measured%20with%20a%20motion%20capture%20system%2C%20and%20we%20want%20the%20joint%20angle(s)%2C%20the%20process%20is%20called%20%5B**inverse%20kinematics**%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FInverse_kinematics).%20For%20the%20one-link%20system%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ctheta%20%3D%20%5Carctan%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7By_P%7D%7Bx_P%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20with%20one%20caveat%20that%20matters%20in%20code.%20The%20ratio%20%24y_P%2Fx_P%24%20is%20the%20same%20for%20a%20point%20and%20for%20its%20mirror%20image%20through%20the%20joint%2C%20so%20the%20plain%20arctangent%20cannot%20tell%20%2445%5Eo%24%20from%20%24-135%5Eo%24.%20The%20two-argument%20function%20%60numpy.arctan2(y%2C%20x)%60%20uses%20the%20signs%20of%20both%20coordinates%20and%20returns%20the%20correct%20angle%20in%20all%20four%20quadrants.%20We%20will%20meet%20this%20again%2C%20with%20consequences%2C%20in%20the%20two-link%20chain.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Matrix%20representation%20of%20the%20kinematics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20algebra%20is%20easier%20in%20matrix%20form%20(and%20let's%20drop%20the%20explicit%20dependence%20on%20%24t%24%20when%20printing)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(G%2C%20r_p%2C%20sym)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20r%20%3D%20sym.Matrix((r_p.dot(G.i)%2C%20r_p.dot(G.j)))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20show(r%2C%20r%22%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D_P%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(r%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20matrix%20form%20simplifies%20things%2C%20but%20we%20lose%20some%20of%20SymPy's%20methods%20for%20vectors%3B%20for%20instance%2C%20the%20vector%20%60r_p%60%20has%20a%20method%20%60magnitude%60%2C%20and%20the%20matrix%20%60r%60%20does%20not.%20If%20you%20prefer%2C%20you%20can%20keep%20the%20vector%20representation%20and%20switch%20to%20the%20matrix%20representation%20only%20to%20display%20a%20variable%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(G%2C%20r_p)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20show(r_p.to_matrix(G)%2C%20r%22%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D_P%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20third%20element%20of%20this%20matrix%20is%20the%20%24%5Chat%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bk%7D%7D%24%20component%2C%20which%20is%20zero%20because%20the%20movement%20is%20planar.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Differential%20kinematics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Differential%20kinematics%20gives%20the%20relationship%20between%20the%20angular%20velocities%20of%20the%20joints%20and%20the%20linear%20velocity%20of%20the%20endpoint.%20This%20mapping%20is%20described%20by%20a%20matrix%2C%20the%20%5B**Jacobian%20matrix**%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FJacobian_matrix_and_determinant)%2C%20which%20depends%20on%20the%20configuration%20of%20the%20chain%20and%20is%20of%20great%20use%20in%20the%20study%20of%20kinematic%20chains.%20First%2C%20let's%20derive%20the%20velocity%20of%20the%20endpoint%20without%20the%20Jacobian%3B%20then%20we%20will%20see%20how%20to%20calculate%20it%20with%20the%20Jacobian.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20velocity%20of%20the%20endpoint%20is%20the%20first-order%20derivative%20of%20its%20position%20vector%2C%20and%20the%20derivative%20of%20a%20vector%20is%20obtained%20by%20differentiating%20each%20of%20its%20components%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Br%7D%7D%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dx_P%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%5C%5C%5B2ex%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dy_P%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20derivative%20is%20with%20respect%20to%20time%2C%20but%20%24x_P%24%20and%20%24y_P%24%20depend%20explicitly%20on%20%24%5Ctheta%24%2C%20and%20it%20is%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20that%20depends%20on%20%24t%24%3A%20%24x_P%24%20and%20%24y_P%24%20depend%20on%20%24t%24%20only%20implicitly.%20To%20calculate%20this%20type%20of%20derivative%20we%20use%20the%20%5Bchain%20rule%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FChain_rule).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20**%5BChain%20rule%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FChain_rule).**%20For%20a%20variable%20%24f%24%20that%20is%20a%20function%20of%20a%20variable%20%24g%24%2C%20which%20in%20turn%20is%20a%20function%20of%20%24t%24%2C%20%24f(g(t))%24%20or%20%24(f%5Ccirc%20g)(t)%24%2C%20the%20derivative%20of%20%24f%24%20with%20respect%20to%20%24t%24%20is%2C%20in%20%5BLagrange's%20notation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FNotation_for_differentiation)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20%24%24(f%5Ccirc%20g)%5E%7B'%7D(t)%20%3D%20f'(g(t))%20%5Ccdot%20g'(t)%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20or%2C%20in%20%5BLeibniz's%20notation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FNotation_for_differentiation)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20%24%24%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Df%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Df%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dg%7D%20%5Ccdot%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dg%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20If%20%24f%24%20is%20a%20function%20of%20two%20variables%20that%20are%20both%20functions%20of%20%24t%24%2C%20%24f(x(t)%2Cy(t))%24%2C%20the%20chain%20rule%20becomes%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20%24%24%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Df%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20f%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20x%7D%20%5Ccdot%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dx%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%2B%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20f%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20y%7D%20%5Ccdot%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dy%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20where%20%24%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Df%2F%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%24%20is%20the%20%5Btotal%20derivative%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FTotal_derivative)%20and%20%24%5Cpartial%20f%20%2F%20%5Cpartial%20x%24%20is%20a%20%5Bpartial%20derivative%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FPartial_derivative).%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20**%5BProduct%20rule%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FProduct_rule).**%20The%20derivative%20of%20the%20product%20of%20two%20functions%20is%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3E%20%24%24%20(f%20%5Ccdot%20g)'%20%3D%20f'%20%5Ccdot%20g%20%2B%20f%20%5Ccdot%20g'%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Linear%20velocity%20of%20the%20endpoint%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20the%20planar%20one-link%20system%2C%20the%20linear%20velocity%20of%20the%20endpoint%20is%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(r%2C%20t)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20v%20%3D%20r.diff(t)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20show(v%2C%20r%22%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(v%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%24%20is%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20joint.%20It%20is%20an%20unknown%20function%20of%20time%2C%20which%20is%20why%20SymPy%20leaves%20it%20as%20a%20derivative%20instead%20of%20evaluating%20it.%20The%20magnitude%2C%20or%20%5BEuclidean%20norm%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FVector_norm)%2C%20of%20the%20vector%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%24%20is%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%7C%7C%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%7C%7C%3D%5Csqrt%7Bv_x%5E2%2Bv_y%5E2%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(sym%2C%20v)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20show(sym.simplify(sym.sqrt(v%5B0%5D%20**%202%20%2B%20v%5B1%5D%20**%202))%2C%20r%22%7C%7C%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%7C%7C%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20That%20is%20%24%5Cell%7C%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%7C%24%3A%20the%20speed%20of%20the%20endpoint%20is%20the%20length%20of%20the%20link%20times%20the%20magnitude%20of%20the%20angular%20velocity%20(SymPy%20does%20not%20know%20the%20sign%20of%20%24%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%24%2C%20so%20it%20keeps%20the%20square%20root%20of%20its%20square).%20We%20could%20have%20used%20SymPy's%20%60norm%60%20method%2C%20but%20the%20output%20does%20not%20simplify%20as%20nicely%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(sym%2C%20v)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20show(sym.simplify(v.norm())%2C%20r%22%7C%7C%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%7C%7C%20%3D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20direction%20of%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7B%5Cmathbf%7Bv%7D%7D%24%20is%20tangent%20to%20the%20circular%20trajectory%20of%20the%20endpoint%2C%20as%20the%20figure%20below%20shows%2C%20together%20with%20the%20components%20of%20the%20velocity.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-2%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fonelink_vel.gif%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D350%20alt%3D%22endpoint%20velocity%20of%20one%20link%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E nt%20coordinates%20%24(x_P%2C%20y_P)%24.%20The%20figure%20below%20shows%20in%20orange%20the%20other%20configuration%20of%20the%20chain%20with%20the%20same%20endpoint.%20The%20other%20solution%20is%20%24%5Ctheta_2'%3D2%5Cpi%20-%20%5Ctheta_2%24%20(equivalently%2C%20%24-%5Ctheta_2%24)%3B%20since%20%24%5Csin(%5Ctheta_2')%3D-%5Csin(%5Ctheta_%7B2%7D)%24%2C%20the%20second%20arctangent%20in%20the%20last%20equation%20changes%20sign.%20Even%20a%20simple%20two-link%20chain%20already%20has%20more%20than%20one%20joint%20configuration%20for%20the%20same%20endpoint%20position%2C%20and%20the%20problem%20gets%20much%20worse%20for%20chains%20with%20more%20links%20(more%20degrees%20of%20freedom).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Ftwolinks_ik.gif%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D350%20alt%3D%22two%20solutions%20of%20the%20inverse%20kinematics%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-5%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Indetermination%20in%20the%20inverse%20kinematics%20of%20a%20two-link%20chain%20with%20hinge%20joints%20in%20a%20plane%3A%20two%20configurations%20reach%20the%20same%20endpoint.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20write%20the%20inverse%20kinematics%20as%20a%20function%2C%20together%20with%20the%20forward%20kinematics%20to%20check%20it.%20As%20announced%20in%20the%20one-link%20section%2C%20the%20code%20uses%20%60arctan2%60%20for%20both%20arctangents%2C%20so%20that%20the%20angles%20come%20out%20right%20in%20every%20quadrant%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20forward_kinematics(theta1%2C%20theta2%2C%20l1%2C%20l2)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Endpoint%20position%20(x%2C%20y)%20of%20a%20planar%20two-link%20chain%20with%20joint%20angles%20in%20radians.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20i d%20the%20body%20and%20a%20hole%20around%20the%20shoulder%20much%20larger%20than%20the%203%20cm%20of%20Exercise%204%3A%20the%20elbow%20cannot%20fold%20the%20hand%20back%20onto%20the%20shoulder.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20There%20is%20a%20neat%20way%20to%20check%20the%20area%2C%20and%20it%20gives%20the%20determinant%20of%20the%20Jacobian%20a%20second%20meaning.%20The%20forward%20kinematics%20maps%20a%20small%20patch%20of%20joint%20space%2C%20%24d%5Ctheta_1%5C%2Cd%5Ctheta_2%24%2C%20to%20a%20small%20patch%20of%20the%20plane%20with%20area%20%24%7C%5Cdet%5Cmathbf%7BJ%7D%7C%5C%2Cd%5Ctheta_1%5C%2Cd%5Ctheta_2%24%3A%20the%20determinant%20is%20the%20factor%20by%20which%20the%20chain%20stretches%20areas.%20Within%20these%20limits%20each%20point%20is%20reached%20by%20a%20single%20posture%2C%20so%20the%20area%20of%20the%20workspace%20is%20the%20integral%20of%20%24%7C%5Cdet%5Cmathbf%7BJ%7D%7C%20%3D%20%5Cell_1%5Cell_2%7C%5Csin%5Ctheta_2%7C%24%20over%20the%20joint%20ranges%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20A%20%3D%20%5Cell_1%5Cell_2%20%5Cint_%7B-30%5Eo%7D%5E%7B135%5Eo%7D%20d%5Ctheta_1%20%5Cint_%7B0%7D%5E%7B145%5Eo%7D%20%5Csin%5Ctheta_2%5C%2C%20d%5Ctheta_2%20%3D%20%5Cell_1%5Cell_2%5C%2C%5CDelta%5Ctheta_1%5C%2C(1%20-%20%5Ccos%20145%5Eo)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20with%20%24%5CDelta%5Ctheta_1%24%20in%20radians%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(L1_arm%2C%20L2_arm%2C%20joint_limits%2C%20np%2C%20workspace_area)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_formula%20%3D%20L1_arm%20*%20L2_arm%20*%20np.ptp(joint_limits%5B0%5D)%20*%20(np.cos(joint_limits%5B1%2C%200%5D)%20-%20np.cos(joint_limits%5B1%2C%201%5D))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Integral%20of%20%7Cdet%20J%7C%3A%20%7B_formula%3A.4f%7D%20m2%3B%20%20random%20points%3A%20%7Bworkspace_area%3A.4f%7D%20m2%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20two%20agree%20to%20within%20the%20random%20error%20of%20the%20400%20000%20points.% %2C%200%5D%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22x%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(ts2%2C%20_term%5B%3A%2C%201%5D%2C%20%22k%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22y%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.set_title(_title)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5B%24s%24%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.locator_params(nbins%3D5)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.grid(True)%0A%20%20%20%20_hax%5B0%5D.set_ylabel(%22Endpoint%20acceleration%20%5B%24m%2Fs%5E2%24%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_hax%5B1%5D.legend(loc%3D%22best%22).get_frame().set_alpha(0.8)%0A%20%20%20%20_fig.suptitle(%22Acceleration%20terms%20for%20the%20minimum-jerk%20trajectory%20of%20a%20two-link%20chain%22%2C%20fontsize%3D16)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20three%20terms%20add%20up%20to%20the%20minimum-jerk%20acceleration%20to%20within%20%2410%5E%7B-15%7D%5C%3B%5Cmathrm%7Bm%2Fs%5E2%7D%24.%20The%20tangential%20term%2C%20the%20one%20produced%20by%20the%20angular%20accelerations%20of%20the%20joints%2C%20is%20the%20largest%2C%20but%20it%20is%20not%20the%20whole%20story.%20The%20centripetal%20term%20reaches%20more%20than%20half%20the%20peak%20of%20the%20total%2C%20and%20the%20Coriolis%20term%20almost%20a%20quarter.%20And%20at%20%24t%20%3D%200.77%24%20s%20the%20tangential%20term%20alone%20is%20larger%20than%20the%20total%20acceleration%3A%20the%20velocity-dependent%20terms%20partly%20cancel%20it.%20To%20produce%20a%20simple%20hand%20acceleration%2C%20the%20joints%20must%20produce%20angular%20accelerations%20that%20compensate%20for%20the%20centripetal%20and%20Coriolis%20accelerations%20the%20movement%20itself%20generates.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Checkpoint%20questions%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Pause%20here%20before%20the%20problems.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Go%20back%20to%20your%20answers%20to%20Challenge%200.%20Did%20your%20shoulder%20and%20elbow%20each%20rotate%20in%20one%20direction%20only%2C%20at%20a%20constant%20rate%3F%20Compare%20with%20the%20simulated%20reach.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20A%20person%20stands%20on%20one%20leg.%20Is%20the%20supporting%20leg%20an%20open%20or%20a%20closed%20kinematic%20chain%20in%20mechanics%3F%20And%20in%20the%20clinical%20sense%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20can%20the%20endpoint%20of%20a%20chain%20accelerate%20when%20no%20joint%20has%20an%20angular%20acceleration%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Why%20does%20the%20Coriolis%20term%20need%20both%20joints%20to%20rotate%2C%20and%20what%20is%20it%20proportional%20to%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Near%20full%20extension%2C%20why%20is%20it%20hard%20to%20move%20the%20hand%20radially%2C%20away%20from%20the%20shoulder%3F%20What%20does%20the%20determinant%20of%20the%20Jacobian%20say%20about%20it%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20A%20planar%20arm%20with%20a%20shoulder%2C%20an%20elbow%20and%20a%20wrist%20moves%20a%20fingertip%20in%20a%20plane.%20What%20is%20its%20mobility%2C%20and%20its%20redundancy%3F%20What%20does%20that%20mean%20for%20the%20inverse%20kinematics%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Calculate%20the%20Jacobian%20matrix%20of%20the%20following%20function%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f(x%2C%20y)%20%3D%20%5Cbegin%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20x%5E2%20y%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%205%20x%20%2B%20%5Csin%20y%20%5Cend%7Bbmatrix%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20For%20the%20two-link%20chain%2C%20calculate%20and%20interpret%20the%20Jacobian%20and%20the%20expressions%20for%20the%20position%2C%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20of%20the%20endpoint%20in%20the%20following%20cases%3A%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a)%20the%20first%20joint%20(the%20joint%20at%20the%20base)%20is%20fixed%20at%20%240%5Eo%24%3B%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b)%20the%20second%20joint%20is%20fixed%20at%20%240%5Eo%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Derive%20the%20equations%20for%20the%20kinematics%20of%20a%20two-link%20pendulum%20with%20the%20angles%20measured%20relative%20to%20the%20vertical.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Derive%20the%20equations%20for%20the%20kinematics%20of%20a%20two-link%20system%20using%20segment%20angles%2C%20and%20compare%20them%20with%20the%20derivation%20using%20joint%20angles.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20For%20the%20two-link%20chain%2C%20a%20special%20case%20of%20movement%20occurs%20when%20the%20endpoint%20moves%20along%20a%20line%20passing%20through%20the%20first%20joint%20(the%20joint%20at%20the%20base).%20A%20system%20with%20this%20behaviour%20is%20known%20as%20a%20polar%20manipulator%20(Mussa-Ivaldi%2C%201986).%20For%20simplicity%2C%20consider%20that%20the%20two%20links%20have%20the%20same%20length%2C%20%24%5Cell%24.%20In%20this%20case%2C%20the%20two%20joint%20angles%20are%20related%20by%20%242%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Ctheta_2%3D%5Cpi%24.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a)%20Calculate%20the%20Jacobian%20of%20this%20polar%20manipulator%20and%20compare%20it%20with%20the%20Jacobian%20of%20the%20standard%20two-link%20chain.%20Note%20the%20difference%20between%20the%20off-diagonal%20terms.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b)%20Calculate%20the%20expressions%20for%20the%20endpoint%20position%2C%20velocity%20and%20acceleration.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20c)%20For%20the%20endpoint%20acceleration%20of%20the%20polar%20manipulator%2C%20identify%20the%20tangential%2C%20centripetal%20and%20Coriolis%20components%2C%20and%20compare%20them%20with%20the%20expressions%20for%20the%20standard%20two-link%20chain.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20%5BEx.%202.22%2C%20Rade's%20book%5D%20In%20an%20internal%20combustion%20engine%2C%20crank%20%24AB%24%2C%20shown%20in%20the%20figure%20below%2C%20rotates%20at%20a%20constant%201000%20rpm%2C%20counterclockwise.%20For%20the%20position%20%24%5Ctheta%3D30%5Eo%24%2C%20determine%3A%20a)%20the%20angular%20velocity%20of%20the%20connecting%20rod%20%24BD%24%3B%20b)%20the%20speed%20of%20the%20piston%20%24P%24.%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fmotor_2rods.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D450%20alt%3D%22crank%2C%20connecting%20rod%20and%20piston%22%2F%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20%5BEx.%202.30%2C%20Rade's%20book%5D%20The%20robot%20shown%20in%20the%20figure%20below%20moves%20in%20a%20plane%2C%20with%20velocity%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7Bv%7D_0%24%20and%20acceleration%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7Ba%7D_0%24%20relative%20to%20the%20floor.%20Arm%20%24O_1O_2%24%20rotates%20with%20angular%20velocity%20%24%5Comega_1%3D%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D_1%24%20and%20angular%20acceleration%20%24%5Calpha_1%3D%5Cddot%7B%5Ctheta%7D_1%24%20relative%20to%20the%20robot's%20body%2C%20and%20arm%20%24O_2P%24%20rotates%20with%20angular%20velocity%20%24%5Comega_2%3D%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D_2%24%20and%20angular%20acceleration%20%24%5Calpha_2%3D%5Cddot%7B%5Ctheta%7D_2%24%20relative%20to%20arm%20%24O_1O_2%24%2C%20in%20the%20directions%20indicated.%20Designating%20by%20%24%5Cell_1%24%20the%20length%20of%20arm%20%24O_1O_2%24%20and%20by%20%24%5Cell_2%24%20the%20length%20of%20arm%20%24O_2P%24%2C%20obtain%20the%20expressions%20for%20the%20velocity%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7Bv%7D_P%24%20and%20the%20acceleration%20%24%5Coverrightarrow%7Ba%7D_P%24%20of%20the%20endpoint%20%24P%24%20relative%20to%20the%20floor%2C%20as%20functions%20of%20the%20indicated%20parameters.%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Frobot_arm.png%3Fraw%3D1%22%20width%3D450%20alt%3D%22planar%20robot%20with%20two%20arms%22%2F%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%208.%20For%20the%20one-link%20minimum-jerk%20movement%20of%20this%20notebook%2C%20find%20the%20instant%20at%20which%20the%20tangential%20and%20centripetal%20accelerations%20of%20the%20endpoint%20have%20the%20same%20magnitude.%20What%20is%20the%20magnitude%20of%20the%20total%20acceleration%20then%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%209.%20Modify%20the%20simulated%20reach%20so%20that%20the%20endpoint%20moves%20in%20a%20straight%20line%20from%20%24(0.3%2C%200.3)%24%20m%20to%20%24(0.65%2C%200.65)%24%20m%2C%20ending%20close%20to%20the%20edge%20of%20the%20workspace.%20Plot%20the%20joint%20angles%20and%20velocities%2C%20and%20explain%20what%20happens%20to%20the%20elbow%20near%20the%20end%20of%20the%20movement%20using%20the%20determinant%20of%20the%20Jacobian.%0A%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20After%20an%20elbow%20injury%2C%20a%20person%20can%20flex%20the%20elbow%20only%20up%20to%20%24100%5Eo%24.%20Using%20the%20arm%20and%20the%20shoulder%20limits%20of%20the%20example%20on%20the%20workspace%20of%20a%20real%20arm%2C%20calculate%20how%20much%20of%20the%20workspace%20is%20lost%2C%20and%20draw%20the%20region%20that%20remains.%20Which%20everyday%20tasks%2C%20done%20with%20the%20hand%20close%20to%20the%20body%2C%20would%20become%20difficult%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%2011.%20Add%20a%20third%20link%20to%20the%20chain%2C%20so%20that%20it%20models%20the%20upper%20arm%2C%20the%20forearm%20and%20the%20hand%2C%20with%20a%20wrist%20joint%3A%20%24%5Cell_1%20%3D%200.30%24%20m%2C%20%24%5Cell_2%20%3D%200.25%24%20m%20and%20%24%5Cell_3%20%3D%200.08%24%20m%20(from%20the%20wrist%20to%20the%20fingertip).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a)%20Write%20the%20forward%20kinematics%20of%20the%20fingertip%20and%20its%20%242%5Ctimes3%24%20Jacobian.%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b)%20At%20%24%5Ctheta_1%20%3D%2030%5Eo%24%2C%20%24%5Ctheta_2%20%3D%2060%5Eo%24%20and%20%24%5Ctheta_3%20%3D%2020%5Eo%24%2C%20find%20a%20combination%20of%20joint%20velocities%20that%20leaves%20the%20fingertip%20still%20(hint%3A%20%60scipy.linalg.null_space%60).%3Cbr%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20c)%20Relate%20the%20result%20to%20the%20redundancy%20of%20the%20chain.%0A%0A%20%20%20%2012.%20The%20quantity%20%24%7C%5Cdet%5Cmathbf%7BJ%7D%7C%24%20is%20sometimes%20used%20as%20a%20measure%20of%20how%20easily%20the%20endpoint%20can%20move%20in%20every%20direction%2C%20the%20manipulability%20of%20the%20chain.%20Plot%20it%20as%20a%20colour%20map%20over%20the%20workspace%20of%20the%20chain%20with%20%24%5Cell_1%20%3D%20%5Cell_2%20%3D%200.5%24%20m.%20Where%20is%20it%20largest%2C%20and%20what%20is%20the%20elbow%20angle%20there%3F%20Is%20that%20where%20you%20would%20choose%20to%20hold%20an%20object%20you%20are%20working%20on%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%2013.%20Inverse%20kinematics%20amplifies%20measurement%20errors%20near%20singular%20configurations.%20For%20the%20chain%20with%20%24%5Cell_1%20%3D%20%5Cell_2%20%3D%200.5%24%20m%2C%20put%20the%20endpoint%20at%200.99%20m%20from%20the%20base%2C%20add%20random%20noise%20with%20a%20standard%20deviation%20of%201%20mm%20to%20its%20coordinates%201000%20times%2C%20and%20calculate%20the%20standard%20deviation%20of%20the%20elbow%20angle%20given%20by%20%60inverse_kinematics%60.%20Repeat%20with%20the%20endpoint%20at%200.70%20m%20from%20the%20base%2C%20and%20explain%20the%20difference%20with%20the%20determinant%20of%20the%20Jacobian.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Final%20answers%20to%20the%20problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20%24J%3D%5B%5B2xy%2Cx%5E2%5D%2C%5B5%2C%5Ccos%20y%5D%5D%24.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Let%20%24u(q)%3D(%5Ccos%20q%2C%5Csin%20q)%24%20and%20%24u_%5Cperp(q)%3D(-%5Csin%20q%2C%5Ccos%20q)%24.%20(a)%20%24r%3D(%5Cell_1%2C0)%2B%5Cell_2u(%5Ctheta_2)%24%2C%20%24v%3D%5Cell_2%5Cdot%5Ctheta_2u_%5Cperp%24%2C%20%24a%3D%5Cell_2%5Cddot%5Ctheta_2u_%5Cperp-%5Cell_2%5Cdot%5Ctheta_2%5E2u%24%3B%20reduced%20Jacobian%20%24%5Cell_2u_%5Cperp%24.%20(b)%20Replace%20the%20chain%20by%20one%20link%20of%20length%20%24%5Cell_1%2B%5Cell_2%24%2C%20angle%20%24%5Ctheta_1%24%3B%20reduced%20Jacobian%20%24(%5Cell_1%2B%5Cell_2)u_%5Cperp(%5Ctheta_1)%24.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20For%20angles%20%24q_1%2Cq_2%24%20measured%20from%20downward%20vertical%20with%20%24q_2%24%20relative%20to%20link%201%3A%20%24r%3D(%5Cell_1%5Csin%20q_1%2B%5Cell_2%5Csin(q_1%2Bq_2)%2C-%5Cell_1%5Ccos%20q_1-%5Cell_2%5Ccos(q_1%2Bq_2))%24.%20The%20velocity%20and%20acceleration%20have%20the%20same%20form%20as%20item%204%20with%20%24u(q)%3D(%5Csin%20q%2C-%5Ccos%20q)%24%20and%20%24u_%5Cperp(q)%3D(%5Ccos%20q%2C%5Csin%20q)%24.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20For%20absolute%20segment%20angles%20%24%5Cphi_1%2C%5Cphi_2%24%3A%20%24r%3D%5Csum_i%5Cell_i%20u(%5Cphi_i)%24%2C%20%24v%3D%5Csum_i%5Cell_i%5Cdot%5Cphi_i%20u_%5Cperp(%5Cphi_i)%24%2C%20%24a%3D%5Csum_i%5Cell_i%5B%5Cddot%5Cphi_i%20u_%5Cperp(%5Cphi_i)-%5Cdot%5Cphi_i%5E2u(%5Cphi_i)%5D%24.%20The%20Jacobian%20columns%20are%20%24%5Cell_i%20u_%5Cperp(%5Cphi_i)%24%3B%20joint%20angles%20obey%20%24%5Cphi_1%3D%5Ctheta_1%24%2C%20%24%5Cphi_2%3D%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Ctheta_2%24.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Under%20the%20stated%20constraint%20there%20is%20one%20independent%20coordinate%20%24q%3D%5Ctheta_1%24%2C%20with%20%24%5Ctheta_2%3D%5Cpi-2q%24.%20Then%20%24r%3D(0%2C2%5Cell%5Csin%20q)%24%2C%20reduced%20%24J%3D(0%2C2%5Cell%5Ccos%20q)%5ET%24%2C%20%24v%3D(0%2C2%5Cell%5Cdot%20q%5Ccos%20q)%24%20and%20%24a%3D(0%2C2%5Cell%5B%5Cddot%20q%5Ccos%20q-%5Cdot%20q%5E2%5Csin%20q%5D)%24.%20The%20net%20transverse%20component%20is%20zero%3B%20the%20full%20unconstrained%20Jacobian%20must%20be%20multiplied%20by%20%24(1%2C-2)%5ET%24%20before%20comparison.%20Separate%20tangential%2C%20centripetal%20and%20Coriolis%20contributions%20depend%20on%20the%20selected%20unconstrained%20coordinates%2C%20although%20their%20sum%20is%20the%20expression%20above.%0A%20%20%20%206.%20%24%5Comega_%7BBD%7D%3D-44.88%24%20rad%2Fs%3B%20piston%20velocity%20%24v_P%3D-8.976%24%20m%2Fs%2C%20with%20the%20signs%20and%20dimensions%20in%20the%20retained%20figure.%0A%20%20%20%207.%20Let%20%24q%3D%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Ctheta_2%24%2C%20%24%5Cdot%20q%3D%5Comega_1%2B%5Comega_2%24%20and%20%24%5Cddot%20q%3D%5Calpha_1%2B%5Calpha_2%24.%20The%20final%20velocity%20is%20%24(v_0%2B%5Cell_1%5Comega_1%5Ccos%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Cell_2%5Cdot%20q%5Ccos%20q%2C%5Cell_1%5Comega_1%5Csin%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Cell_2%5Cdot%20q%5Csin%20q)%24.%20Acceleration%20is%20%24(a_0%2B%5Cell_1%5B%5Calpha_1%5Ccos%5Ctheta_1-%5Comega_1%5E2%5Csin%5Ctheta_1%5D%2B%5Cell_2%5B%5Cddot%20q%5Ccos%20q-%5Cdot%20q%5E2%5Csin%20q%5D%2C%5Cell_1%5B%5Calpha_1%5Csin%5Ctheta_1%2B%5Comega_1%5E2%5Ccos%5Ctheta_1%5D%2B%5Cell_2%5B%5Cddot%20q%5Csin%20q%2B%5Cdot%20q%5E2%5Ccos%20q%5D)%24.%0A%20%20%20%208.%20Nontrivial%20interior%20instants%200.357325%20and%200.642675%20s%3B%20acceleration%20magnitude%208.73409%20m%2Fs%C2%B2%20at%20each.%20At%20the%20endpoints%20both%20components%20are%20also%20zero.%0A%20%20%20%209.%20End%20elbow%20flexion%20is%20about%2046.37%C2%B0%20for%20the%20positive-elbow%20solution%2C%20compared%20with%20about%20129.79%C2%B0%20initially.%20The%20Jacobian%20determinant%20decreases%20near%20the%20outer%20boundary%2C%20increasing%20sensitivity%20to%20endpoint%20errors%3B%20minimum-jerk%20endpoint%20speed%20still%20goes%20to%20zero%20at%20the%20end.%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20Remaining%20area%200.334607%20m%C2%B2%3B%20area%20lost%200.184033%20m%C2%B2%2C%20about%2035.5%25%20of%20the%20original%20workspace.%20The%20lost%20region%20is%20mainly%20close%20to%20the%20shoulder%3B%20bringing%20the%20hand%20to%20the%20mouth%20or%20chest%20becomes%20more%20difficult.%0A%20%20%20%2011.%20With%20%24%5Cphi_i%3D%5Csum_%7Bk%5Cle%20i%7D%5Ctheta_k%24%2C%20%24r%3D%5Csum_i%5Cell_i%20u(%5Cphi_i)%24%20and%20%24J_%7B%3A%2Cj%7D%3D%5Csum_%7Bi%5Cge%20j%7D%5Cell_i%20u_%5Cperp(%5Cphi_i)%24.%20A%20unit%20null-space%20velocity%20is%20approximately%20%24(0.072823%2C-0.324444%2C0.943097)%24%20rad%2Fs%2C%20or%20any%20scalar%20multiple.%20The%20fingertip%20has%20two%20position%20constraints%20and%20three%20joint%20rates%2C%20leaving%20one%20generic%20redundant%20direction.%0A%20%20%20%2012.%20Maximum%20%24%7C%5Cdet%20J%7C%3D0.25%24%20m%C2%B2%20at%20elbow%20angles%20%C2%B190%C2%B0%2C%20on%20radius%20%24%5Csqrt%7B0.5%7D%3D0.707107%24%20m.%20This%20is%20best%20for%20the%20stated%20kinematic%20area%20measure%3B%20comfort%2C%20strength%20and%20load%20direction%20also%20affect%20a%20useful%20working%20posture.%0A%20%20%20%2013.%20With%20NumPy%20generator%20seed%200%20and%201000%20independent%20coordinate-noise%20samples%2C%20elbow-angle%20standard%20deviations%20are%20about%200.828%C2%B0%20at%200.99%20m%20and%200.164%C2%B0%20at%200.70%20m.%20The%20near-extended%20posture%20has%20the%20smaller%20determinant%20and%20greater%20amplification.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(L1_arm%2C%20L2_arm%2C%20mo%2C%20np%2C%20plt)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_t%3Dnp.linspace(0%2C1%2C501)%3B_s%3D10*_t**3-15*_t**4%2B6*_t**5%0A%20%20%20%20_x%3D.3%2B.35*_s%3B_y%3D_x.copy()%0A%20%20%20%20_q1%2C_q2%3Dinverse_kinematics(_x%2C_y%2C.5%2C.5%2Celbow%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20_fig%2C_ax%3Dplt.subplots(1%2C3%2Cfigsize%3D(12%2C3.5))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax%5B0%5D.plot(_t%2Cnp.degrees(np.c_%5B_q1%2C_q2%5D))%3B_ax%5B0%5D.set(xlabel%3D%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22%2Cylabel%3D%22Joint%20angle%20%5Bdeg%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax%5B1%5D.plot(_t%2Cnp.degrees(np.gradient(np.c_%5B_q1%2C_q2%5D%2C_t%2Caxis%3D0)))%3B_ax%5B1%5D.set(xlabel%3D%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22%2Cylabel%3D%22Joint%20rate%20%5Bdeg%2Fs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_a%2C_b%3Dnp.meshgrid(np.linspace(-30%2C135%2C160)%2Cnp.linspace(0%2C100%2C120))%3B_a%3Dnp.radians(_a)%3B_b%3Dnp.radians(_b)%0A%20%20%20%20_xx%3DL1_arm*np.cos(_a)%2BL2_arm*np.cos(_a%2B_b)%3B_yy%3DL1_arm*np.sin(_a)%2BL2_arm*np.sin(_a%2B_b)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax%5B2%5D.scatter(_xx.ravel()%2C_yy.ravel()%2Cs%3D1%2Calpha%3D.25)%3B_ax%5B2%5D.set(xlabel%3D%22X%20%5Bm%5D%22%2Cylabel%3D%22Y%20%5Bm%5D%22%2Caspect%3D%22equal%22%2Ctitle%3D%22Elbow%20limit%20100%C2%B0%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax%5B0%5D.legend(%5B%22shoulder%22%2C%22elbow%22%5D)%3B_ax%5B1%5D.legend(%5B%22shoulder%22%2C%22elbow%22%5D)%3B_fig.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20_problem_plot%20%3D%20mo
